newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GM sees strong new car sales in southeast Europe.
newsitem.headline: GM sees strong new car sales in southeast Europe.

text.p: New auto sales in nine countries in southeast Europe together will rise 50 percent to 390,010 units in 2000 from 259,600 units in 1996, U.S. automaker General Motors Corp said on Thursday.
"This region will offer significant growth opportunities for GM," said Christopher Lacey, marketing and sales director at Opel Hungary Ltd (OH), a division of GM's German automaker Adam Opel AG.
"In this period, our market share should grow from eight percent to 11 percent."

Lacey spoke at a news conference to announce the creation of an Opel subsidiary, Opel Southeast Europe Ltd, to handle marketing and sales in the region that he said includes Albania, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Hungary, Macedonia, Romania, Slovenia and Yugoslavia.
In Hungary alone, sales of new autos will grow seven percent to 94,500 units in 1997 from 88,348 units in 1996, Lacey forecast.
"Opel will maintain a market share between 18 and 20 percent in Hungary next year," he said, noting Opel has kept a share above 20 percent as the top-selling brand in Hungary since 1994.

At Opel Hungary's plants, engine production will rise above 400,000 units in 1997, compared with 310,000 units in 1996, while car assembly this year will roughly match output of 11,250 units last year, the company's managing director Albert Lidauer said at the news conference.

"The number of export destinations for our engines will increase as production at our new cylinder-head facility accelerates," he said, adding that Opel Hungary delivers engines to eight GM car assembly plants in five countries. (( -- Ryan Tutak, Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040 ))
